# 数据卡（Data Card）
## 基本信息
| 项 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 数据集名称 | Viewpoint-Aware Pig Posture Recognition Dataset |
| 维护者 | Anil Bhujel（HuggingFace 账号 anilbhujel） |
| 获取地址 | https://huggingface.co/datasets/anilbhujel/viewpoint-aware-pig-posture-recognition |
| 许可 | CC BY 4.0 |
| 本项目使用的划分 | seenVPtest.csv + seenVPtest_images/（官方测试划分之一） |
| 本项目构建日期 | 2026-10-19 |
| 构建脚本 | scripts/build_dataset.py（确定性，可用 SHA256 校验复现） |
## 采集背景（依据数据集 README）
采集自 2 个真实猪栏，每栏 4 台相机：2 台鱼眼顶装（1280×720）、
2 台 Orbbec Femto RGB（1920×1080）；
标注为逐实例：bbox（XYWH 像素）+ class_id + 相机视角角（方位角/仰角，
由 PnP 标定推算）；
相机坐标系与视角角定义见原 README（zenith 约定：0° 为正上方，90° 为水平）。
## 标签体系
| class_id | 原始标签 | 含义 | 本项目规范类别 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Laterallyingleft | 左侧卧 | lying_lateral |

title: data_card.md
text:
| 1 | Laterallyingright | 右侧卧 | lying_lateral |
| 2 | Sitting | 坐姿 | sitting |
| 3 | Standing | 站立 | standing |
| 4 | Sternallying | 胸腹着地俯卧 | lyingother |
合并说明：
左/右侧卧合并为 lying_lateral，因为本任务的目标是姿态识别而非朝向判定；
Sternallying 映射为 lyingother，与提示词中"躯干着地但不符合侧卧定义"一致。
## 本项目的数据处理
1. 只取测试划分：避免与数据集作者的监督训练集重叠，也避免我们自己"训练"任何模型
（本项目不训练模型，仅用 API）。
2. 选择性下载：先用 CSV 贪心选图（53 张），再只下载这些源图（≈9.8 MB），
不下载 6000+ 文件的完整数据集。
3. 逐实例裁剪：向外扩 8% 边距，使单只猪完整且带少量上下文。
4. 质量过滤：短边 ≥64px、面积 ≥8192px²、长宽比 ≤4:1。共排除 3 个实例。
5. 按源图分组划分：同源图的裁切强制同 split，避免近重复泄漏；
种子 20261019，dev 0.2 / test 0.8。
6. 分层限量：test 不超过 200 条，按类别比例抽样。
## 规模与分布（实测）
| split | 总数 | standing | lyinglateral | lyingother | sitting | 源图数 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| dev | 109 | 44 | 24 | 36 | 5 | 12 |

title: data_card.md
text:
| test | 200 | 78 | 62 | 47 | 13 | 41 |
裁切尺寸（test 集）：短边最小 66px、中位 169px、最大 324px；短边 <128px 占 27.5%。
## 已知偏差与限制
| 偏差 | 影响 | 缓解 |
|---|---|---|
| 类别不均衡：sitting 在测试集仅 13 条 | 该类指标方差大 | 报告中逐类报告并注明样本量，不下强结论 |
| 裁切图偏小（27.5% 短边 <128px） | 细节不足，模型可能依赖轮廓与地面接触关系 | 上采样到 512px 再送入模型；在局限性中说明 |
| 同源图多裁切共享背景/光照 | 统计独立性弱于独立拍摄 | 按源图分组划分；报告源图数量 |
| 仅 2 个猪栏、8 台相机 | 跨场泛化未验证 | 明确声明适用范围 |
| 单一物种/日龄段的商品猪 | 不能外推到母猪、仔猪 | 声明 |
## 隐私与合规
数据为公开数据集，许可允许研究与再分发（需署名）；
不含人员面部或可识别个人信息；
裁切图会通过公网发送至模型服务商进行处理，使用前请确认该行为符合你的要求。

# 实验报告：提示词设计对多模态大模型猪只姿态识别的影响
实验已完成。本报告所有数字均由 results/raw/testmainv2_raw.csv（600 条真实调用记录）
经 scripts/plot_results.py 计算得到，可用同一命令复算。
生成日期：2026-10-19
## 0. 结论速览
| 研究问题 | 结论 |
|---|---|
| RQ1 大模型能否识别猪只姿态？ | 能力有限。最佳方案准确率 37.7%，仅略高于四分类随机水平 25%，Macro-F1 仅 0.232 |
| RQ2 明确姿态定义能否提升表现？ | 不能。B 组（0.370）与 A 组（0.377）几乎无差异（差 0.7 个百分点） |
| RQ3 强制 JSON + 允许拒答能否改善可靠性？ | 一半成功：JSON 有效率从 0% 提升到 99.5%；但模型一次拒答都没有使用（unknown 率 0%） |
| RQ4 典型错误与边界？ | 模型存在严重的"侧卧"先验（80%+ 预测为 lying_lateral），sitting 一次未预测，standing 召回率仅 13–28% |
最重要的发现是一个负面结果：增加提示词约束能显著改善输出格式，
但没有改善、甚至略微降低了分类准确率（C 组最低）。
## 1. 实验目的与研究问题
比较三组提示词设计对猪只姿态识别的影响，区分三个维度：
分类正确性（Accuracy / Macro-F1）
结构化输出质量（JSON 有效率）
不确定性处理（拒答率）

## 9. 结果分析与讨论
## 9.1 RQ1：模型能否识别姿态？——能力有限
四分类随机水平 25%，三个方案分别为 37.7% / 37.0% / 33.0%，
只比随机猜测好一点；Macro-F1 0.167–0.232 也说明各类别表现极不均衡。
但要注意：这不等于模型"看不懂猪"。从 description 字段看，
模型对画面的描述大体合理（"身体侧面贴地，躯干呈水平姿态"），
它的问题在于类别判别粒度，而不是完全无法理解图像。
## 9.2 RQ2：明确姿态定义有用吗？——没有

title: experiment_report.md
section: 9.2 RQ2：明确姿态定义有用吗？——没有
text:
A（0.377）vs B（0.370）相差 0.7 个百分点，在 200 样本上属于噪声范围
（单个样本约 0.5 个百分点）。混淆矩阵显示两者的错误模式几乎相同。
合理的解释：模型已经把猪识别为"躺着的猪"，但**从俯视鱼眼视角无法可靠区分
站立 / 侧卧 / 俯卧**——这些区分依赖地面接触、腿部伸展、阴影等线索，
而裁切图是正上方俯拍，腿常被躯干遮挡。增加文字定义无法弥补视觉证据的缺失。
## 9.3 RQ3：JSON 约束与拒答规则——一半成功
格式方面：完全成功。 JSON 有效率从 0%（A/B）提升到 99.5%（C，199/200）。
说明"明确字段 + 只许 JSON + 禁止多余文字"这套约束对输出格式非常有效。
不确定性处理：完全失败。 C 组明确允许在证据不足时返回 unknown，
但 600 次调用中 uncertain=true 出现 0 次，unknown 预测 0 次。
模型宁可给一个（很可能错的）具体类别，也不愿拒答。
这一点很重要：提示词能约束格式，但约束不了"诚实"。
若要用拒答机制做质量门控，可能需要更强的干预（如前置置信度阈值、
两阶段调用、或改用支持结构化置信度的接口），单靠提示词不可靠。
## 9.4 RQ4：为什么 C 组更差？
C 组准确率最低（0.330），且 standing 召回从 28.2%（A）掉到 12.8%。
一个可能的原因是长定义带来的锚定效应：C 组对 lying_lateral 的描述较详细
（"身体一侧着地，躯干长轴大致水平贴地，通常可见一侧体侧"），
与俯视图下的猪体外形高度吻合，模型更容易把所有猪都判成侧卧
（预测分布：A 159 → B 161 → C 179 条 lying_lateral）。

title: experiment_report.md
section: 9.4 RQ4：为什么 C 组更差？
text:
这是"提示词越详细越好"这一直觉的反例：更长的定义可能强化错误的视觉先验。
## 9.5 三组一致性
三组预测完全相同的样本占 170/200（85%）；A 与 B 不同的仅 19 条，
A 与 C 不同的 21 条。提示词改变的主要是格式，而不是判断。
这与 8.1 中三者准确率接近、8.3 中混淆模式雷同的观察一致。
## 10. 典型错误案例
| 错误类型 | 典型表现 | 数量（C 组） |
|---|---|---:|
| 站立 → 侧卧 | 站立猪被判成侧卧，模型描述"身体一侧贴地" | 67 / 78 |
| 俯卧 → 侧卧 | 胸腹着地被判成侧卧 | 43 / 47 |
| 坐姿 → 侧卧 | 坐姿样本无一判对 | 13 / 13 |
| 侧卧 → 站立 | 反向误判，较少 | 6 / 62 |
| 完全无法解析 | 一次未能抽出任何类别 | 1 / 600 |
目视复核两张被判为侧卧的"站立"样本（testpen1turcam2202509210517260003/0004）：
从正上方俯拍，猪体轮廓呈长条贴地状，四肢几乎不可见，其中后者仅 158×104 像素。
在这种视角与分辨率下，人类标注者如果不借助时间上下文与地面阴影，也很难仅凭单帧判断站立与否。
这说明部分错误源于任务本身在俯视图下的不可辨识性，不能全部归咎于模型。
## 11. 实验局限性
1. 样本量小：200 条测试样本，sitting 仅 13 条；单样本约 0.5 个百分点，
A/B 之间 0.7 个百分点的差异不能视为真实差异；
2. 单次运行：未做重复实验，无法区分"能力差异"与"采样噪声"（可用 --repeats）；

title: experiment_report.md
text:
3. 单一模型：结论只适用于 glm-4.1v-thinking-flash，不能外推到其它 VLM；
4. 裁切输入 + 俯视视角：任务难度被视角放大，指标不可与整帧多目标研究直接比较；
5. 标签来源：使用数据集作者标注，未做二次人工核验，未计算标注一致性 κ；
6. 免费模型：限流与排队影响响应时间（p95 达 8.9s），但不影响分类结果的正确性判断；
7. 二次解析：修正解析器后重算了指标，虽然只改文本抽取、未改原始返回，
但严格来说初版与修正版的数字不同，已在第 7 节完整披露。
## 12. 结论与改进方向
结论
1. 在俯视鱼眼视角的单猪裁切图上，该视觉大模型的姿态识别准确率为 33%–38%，
仅略高于 25% 的随机水平，不足以支撑生产使用；
2. 提示词中增加类别定义没有提升准确率（RQ2 否定），
过度详细的定义甚至可能强化错误先验（C 组最差）；
3. 提示词能有效约束输出格式（JSON 有效率 0% → 99.5%），
但无法诱导模型诚实拒答（拒答率 0%）——格式可控、可靠性不可控；
4. 主要错误集中在"站立/俯卧 → 侧卧"的单向塌缩，源自俯视图下姿态线索不足。
改进方向
1. 换用包含侧视/斜视角度的数据（如数据集的 Orbbec 机位）或 unseen-VP 划分，
检验视角是否是主要瓶颈；
2. 提供上下文（如同一场景的多帧、或标注框外的地面阴影）帮助判别；
3. 用 --repeats 做重复实验并给出置信区间，而非单次比较；
4. 引入"置信度阈值 + 两阶段复核"替代纯提示词的拒答机制；
5. 增加第二标注者计算 κ，区分"模型错"与"标签有争议"；

title: experiment_report.md
text:
6. 把"能否拒答"作为独立实验（例如强制二选一 vs 允许 unknown）单独检验。

title: technical_report.md
text:
# 技术报告：基于多模态大语言模型的猪只姿态识别与可见体态描述系统
版本：2026-10-19 运行环境：Windows + Python 3.9.25（conda data_science 环境）
说明：本报告描述已实现并已测试的系统。涉及模型能力与实验结论的部分见
实验报告，其中未运行的部分明确标注「待实验」。
## 1. 项目背景与需求分析
## 1.1 背景
猪只姿态（站立、侧卧、俯卧、坐姿）是养殖场巡检中可直接观察的表型信息，
也是行为监测与福利评估的基础。传统方案需要训练专用视觉模型；而多模态大模型
（VLM）提供了"零样本/少样本 + 语义解释"的替代路径。
本项目定位为应用层原型：不做模型训练或微调，而是围绕云端 VLM API 构建
一条可复用、可评测的流水线，并用对照实验回答"提示词设计能带来多少收益"。
## 1.2 需求拆解
| 需求（说明书） | 本项目的落实方式 |
|---|---|
| 3.1 上传本地图片 | POST /api/predict multipart 上传，格式与尺寸校验 |
| 3.1 调用视觉模型 API | src/vision_client.py，OpenAI 兼容协议 |
| 3.1 识别姿态 + 可见体态描述 | 结构化 Schema（posture / description / uncertain / uncertainty_reason） |
| 3.1 结构化输出 | 提示词约束 + 本地解析 + Schema 校验（无原生 JSON 模式） |
| 3.1 展示结果与不确定性 | Web 界面右侧面板，展示类别、描述、不确定性、状态、耗时 |

title: technical_report.md
text:
| 3.1 读取人工标注数据集并批量评测 | scripts/builddataset.py + src/experimentrunner.py |
| 3.1 指标计算与结果导出 | src/evaluation.py，输出指标 CSV、逐类明细、混淆矩阵 |
| 3.1 安装/运行/复现说明 | README.md、requirements.txt、docs/ |
| 6.2 三组提示词 | prompts/prompt_{a,b,c}.txt，运行时计算 SHA256 入档 |
| 6.4 指标 | Accuracy（两种口径）、Macro-F1、JSON 有效率、拒答率、耗时、失败率 |
| 6.6 可视化 | src/reporting.py 生成 7 张图（含混淆矩阵） |
| 7.3 密钥管理 | .env + 环境变量；.env.example 仅占位符；.env 在 .gitignore |
| 3.3 禁止扩大范围 | 未实现训练、巡检机器人、视频流、用户系统、疾病诊断 |
## 2. 系统总体架构
数据流：图片 → 校验 → EXIF 纠正 → 长边缩放 512px → JPEG 重编码 →
Base64 Data URI → chat/completions → 原始文本 → 解析 → Schema 校验 →
逐条记录 CSV → 指标 → 图表/报告。
## 3. 技术选型与理由
| 层 | 选型 | 理由 | 与需求建议的差异 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 语言 | Python 3.9.25 | 本机现成环境，零安装 | 需求建议 3.10+，如实记录差异 |

title: technical_report.md
text:
| Web | tornado 6.5.1 | 已随 Jupyter 安装；支持 multipart 与异步 | 用自写单页替代 Gradio |
| 测试 | unittest（标准库） | 零安装，能力等价 | 替代 pytest |
| 配置 | 自写 .env 解析（30 行） | 零安装 | 替代 python-dotenv |
| 图像 | Pillow 11.3.0 | EXIF、缩放、裁剪齐备 | — |
| 数据 | pandas 2.3.3 / numpy | 表格与数值 | — |
| 指标 | 纯 Python 手算 + sklearn 交叉核对 | 口径可控、可审计 | 需求建议 sklearn，本项目把它当"第二实现" |
| 图表 | matplotlib 3.9.2（Agg + 微软雅黑） | 中文无豆腐块 | — |
| 模型 | 智谱 glm-4.6v-flash（免费） | 无需充值，降低课程成本 | 需求建议 Qwen-VL/GLM，二者均实现 |
实际使用的模型：最终实验采用 glm-4.1v-thinking-flash（同样免费）。
原因是实测发现 glm-4.6v-flash 在当前网络下限流严重（模型级拥堵，单次验证 8 张仅 3 张成功、
即使退避 137 秒仍会失败），而 glm-4.1v-thinking-flash 在同样条件下 8/8 成功、
正式实验 600 次调用零失败。三组提示词全程使用同一个模型，控制变量成立。
为什么不用 Gradio：gradio==4.44.1 要求 pillow<11，会把环境中的

title: technical_report.md
text:
pillow 11.3.0 降级，影响同环境下其它项目；新版 gradio 需要 Python ≥3.10。
需求说明书明确允许"若某个库与当前 Python 环境不兼容，应选择简单、稳定的替代方案，
并在文档中说明"。因此改用 tornado，接口层与 UI 层解耦，未来替换成本低。
## 4. 核心模块设计
## 4.1 config.py —— 配置
.env 自解析：忽略注释/空行、支持 export 、剥除成对引号；
优先级：进程环境变量 > .env > 默认值；
密钥缺失时抛 MissingAPIKeyError，消息为可操作的中文提示；
数值型配置非法时抛 ConfigError 并指出变量名。
## 4.2 src/schema.py —— 结果契约
| 字段 | 类型 | 约束 |
|---|---|---|
| posture | enum | standing / lyinglateral / lyingother / sitting / unknown |
| description | string | 非空；>500 字仅告警不判非法 |
| uncertain | bool | 必须为布尔（接受 "true"/"false" 字符串并记录） |
| uncertainty_reason | string \| null | 类型不符判非法 |
一致性规则：posture=unknown 且 uncertain=false → 记 warning。
中文同义词（"侧卧""站立""趴卧"…）与混合写法（standing（站立））都能归一化。
数据集 5 类 → 4 类的映射集中在此模块，避免各处硬编码。

title: technical_report.md
text:
## 4.3 src/output_parser.py —— 解析与降级
解析前先做推理过程剥离：本实验使用的思考型模型会输出
<think>推理</think><answer>结论</answer>，推理里常出现与结论相反或半截的类别词。
因此先移除 <think> 块，若存在 <answer> 则只解析其内容，避免推理污染结果。
在此基础上级联解析：
1. json.loads 直接解析；
2. 剥离 围栏 → 括号配对扫描（正确处理字符串内的 {}` 与转义引号）→ 再解析；
3. 轻量修补（智能引号、尾随逗号、Python 字面量、单引号键值）→ 再解析；
4. 正则逐字段抽取，标记 json_valid=false；
5. 自由文本抽取：从自然语言回答中抄出出现的规范类别词（A/B 组即此种情形），
只抄写不推断，找不到类别词就返回失败；
6. 全部失败 → method=failed，不产生任何伪造字段。
jsonvalid（能否解析出 JSON 对象）与 schemavalid（字段是否合规）分开统计，
便于区分"格式失败"与"内容错误"。
## 4.4 src/vision_client.py —— API 客户端
统一 OpenAI 兼容协议；buildmessages 生成 imageurl + text 双块；
错误分类：401/403/400 不重试（重试无意义），408/429/5xx/超时/连接错误
指数退避重试（尊重 Retry-After，上限 30–60s）；
私有参数（智谱 thinking）若被服务端拒绝，自动去掉后重试一次并记录；
令牌桶限流（默认 1 QPS），线程安全；

title: technical_report.md
text:
返回 ModelResponse，失败也返回对象而不是抛异常，便于逐条落盘。
## 4.5 src/experiment_runner.py —— 批量编排
ThreadPoolExecutor 并发；每线程复用 session（threading.local）；
逐条 append + flush + fsync，进程崩溃后可按 (sample_id, variant) 续跑；
maxcalls 硬闸：达到上限后取消剩余任务，并在摘要中报告 naborted 与停止原因；
记录 24 个字段（见 §6.2），含模型原始返回 raw_text 以便审计；
失败样本照样落盘，不会被静默丢弃。
## 4.6 src/evaluation.py —— 指标
口径写死在文件头注释里，并由单元测试逐项校验：
| 指标 | 分母 |
|---|---|
| 调用失败率 | 全部记录 |
| JSON 有效率 | 全部记录（需 jsonvalid && schemavalid） |
| 无法判断比例 | 成功调用数 |
| Accuracy（有效） | 成功 且抽出了合法类别的样本 |
| Accuracy（严格） | 全部记录（拒答/失败算错） |
| 每类 Precision / Recall / F1 | 有效分类子集 |
| recall_strict | 该类全部样本（含拒答） |
| Macro-F1 | 四类 F1 等权平均 |
| 延迟 mean / median / p95 | 成功调用（最近秩法） |
关键口径：分类得分不要求 Schema 合规。A/B 组是自然语言输出、C 组是严格 JSON；

title: technical_report.md
text:
如果把"Schema 合规"作为得分前提，A/B 的分类能力就完全无法比较，
格式劣势会被误记为识别能力劣势。因此两者分开统计——格式由"JSON 有效率"衡量，
正确性由 Accuracy/Macro-F1 衡量。这一口径由单元测试锁定。
## 5. 多模态 API 接入方式
要点：
图片以 Base64 Data URI 内联，不依赖公网 URL，避免图床上传与隐私问题；
送入前统一缩放到长边 512px，估算单图 ≈258 视觉 Token（32×32 px/Token）；
thinking=disabled 关闭思考链，降低延迟与输出 Token；
视觉接口没有原生 JSON Schema 约束，因此采用"提示词强制 + 本地校验"，
并把 JSON 有效率作为被评测的指标而不是前提假设。
## 6. 提示词管理与结构化输出
## 6.1 三组提示词
| 组 | 文件 | 特征 | 字符数 | SHA256 前 8 位 |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| A | prompts/prompt_a.txt | 只给任务、类别列表与简短输出要求 | 124 | 098f7653 |
| B | prompts/prompt_b.txt | 增加各类定义、易混淆区分规则、只依据可见信息 | 484 | 914878c3 |
| C | prompts/prompt_c.txt | 再增加严格 JSON 字段、只允许 5 个取值、允许拒答、禁止虚构 | 946 | e5c513d4 |
SHA256 在每次运行前重算并写入原始记录与实验元数据，保证报告引用的提示词
与实际调用完全一致（可追溯）。
## 6.2 逐样本记录字段

title: technical_report.md
text:
字段覆盖需求 6.5 建议的全部字段，并补充 schema_valid（区分解析与校验）、
promptsha256（提示词可追溯）、rawtext（原始响应审计）。
## 7. 异常处理与数据安全
| 场景 | 处理 |
|---|---|
| 无密钥 | 界面/脚本给出中文提示并停止；绝不返回假结果 |
| 401/403 | 不重试，提示检查密钥 |
| 429 | 退避重试并提示可降低 QPS/并发 |
| 5xx / 超时 / 连接错误 | 指数退避重试（默认 3 次） |
| 返回空内容 | 记为失败，不编造 |
| 非 JSON 返回 | 三级降级解析；仍失败则记失败并保留原文 |
| 字段非法/类别越界 | Schema 判非法，predicted_label 留空 |
| 图片损坏/过小/超长宽比 | 上传前拦截，中文报错，且不发起 API 调用 |
| 调用失败 | 保留失败记录并计入失败率 |
| 磁盘写入 | 逐条 append + fsync；CSV 使用 utf-8-sig 保证 Excel 不乱码 |
| 密钥泄漏 | 密钥只从环境/.env 读取；.env 在 .gitignore；日志不打印密钥 |
数据安全：图片会发送至所选服务商处理，README 与界面横幅均有提示；
仅使用公开且许可允许的数据集（CC BY 4.0）。
## 8. 系统实现与界面
单页界面：深色主题，左侧上传区 + 提示词下拉，右侧结果面板；
结果面板展示：姿态（中英）、可见体态描述、不确定性及原因、调用状态、
HTTP 码、模型耗时与含上传的总耗时、Token 用量、图片尺寸变化与视觉 Token 估算、
提示词方案与 SHA256 前缀、模型原始返回（可展开）；

title: technical_report.md
text:
状态徽章：调用成功/失败、Schema 通过/未通过、JSON 有效/无效、存在不确定性；
顶部横幅常驻说明当前服务商与"图片将发送至该服务商"；
无 CDN 依赖，全部资源内联，可离线加载页面。
已实测的接口（真实 HTTP 请求，非模拟）：
| 请求 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| GET / | 200，返回完整单页 HTML（9554 字节） |
| GET /api/health | 200，返回服务商/模型/密钥状态/提示词列表 |
| GET /api/prompts | 200，返回三组提示词全文与 SHA256 |
| GET /api/nothing | 404，返回 JSON 错误体（非 HTML） |
| POST /api/predict（无密钥） | 200，ok=false、need_key=true、中文原因 |
| POST /api/predict（非图片文件） | 返回中文"无法识别"且未发起 API 调用 |
| POST /api/predict（5×5 小图） | 返回"尺寸过小" |
## 9. 测试方案与测试结果
## 9.1 方案
框架：标准库 unittest，全部为可离线执行的测试；
真实 API 调用由 scripts/verify_api.py 单独负责，避免测试污染额度；
网页测试使用 tornado 的 AsyncHTTPTestCase，起真实 HTTP 服务但模型调用打桩。
## 9.2 实际运行结果
| 测试文件 | 用例数 | 覆盖内容 |
|---|---:|---|

title: technical_report.md
text:
| testoutputparser.py | 36 | 直接/围栏/夹叙/修补/单引号/正则降级/自由文本/推理块剥离/失败/截断/数组 |
| test_schema.py | 18 | 枚举归一化（中英/混合/标点）、类别映射、四字段校验、一致性告警 |
| test_config.py | 9 | .env 解析、缺密钥中文提示、默认值、非法数值、服务商切换 |
| testimageutils.py | 23 | 格式/损坏/过小/超长宽比/超大、EXIF、RGBA、缩放、裁剪、质量阈值 |
| testvisionclient_errors.py | 18 | 成功路径、载荷结构、401/403 不重试、429/500/超时/连接错误、空返回、thinking 参数、限流 |
| test_evaluation.py | 17 | 手算逐项核对、sklearn 交叉验证、拒答/失败/空集、混淆矩阵、延迟分位 |
| testexperimentrunner.py | 8 | 记录字段完整性、失败落盘、不可解析不伪造、续跑、成本闸、样本加载 |
| test_manifest.py | 7 | 贪心选图、按图分组划分、确定性、分层限量 |
| test_webapp.py | 9 | 首页、health、prompts、404、缺少文件、缺密钥、非图片、小图、打桩透传 |
| test_reporting.py | 3 | 图表生成、Markdown 含真实数字、空数据不产图 |
| 合计 | 148 | — |
说明：以上 148 项均为模拟测试（模型调用被 HTTP 打桩替换），可离线执行。
真实 API 集成测试见 9.3 节。

title: technical_report.md
text:
## 9.3 真实 API 集成验证（非模拟）
| 项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 阶段一验证 scripts/verifyapi.py --count 8 | 8/8 成功，原始响应存于 results/verification/verifyC20261019130234.json |
| 端点鉴权 | HTTP 200，鉴权通过 |
| 正式实验 | 600 次调用，0 失败，耗时 26.1 分钟，共 388,407 Token |
| 结果可复现 | plotresults.py 从原始 CSV 重算，指标与首次计算逐字段一致** |
| 故障注入（模拟测试） | 401/403 不重试、429 退避后成功、5xx/超时按策略失败、坏 JSON 走降级 — 全部符合预期 |
解析链路上真实遇到过的两种模型行为，均已覆盖并修复：
1. 思考型输出：模型返回 <think>推理</think><answer>结论</answer>，
推理中常出现与结论相反或半截的类别词 → 解析前剥离 <think>，优先解析 <answer>；
2. 类别词写法漂移：模型把 lying_lateral 写成 lying lateral 或 lying-other
→ 正则允许空格/连字符并归一化。
第 2 点曾导致 A 组 8 条被判"无法解析"。修正后新增 scripts/reparse_results.py，
可在不重新调用 API 的前提下，对已有原始记录重新抽取字段并重算指标
（原始 raw_text 不改动，输入输出文件分离，改动幅度会打印出来供核对）。
本项目实际重解析后可用样本从 590/600 提升到 599/600。
## 9.4 其他工程验证

title: technical_report.md
text:
数据集确定性：在 PYTHONHASHSEED=0/12345/999 下重复构建，
manifest.csv 的 SHA256 完全一致（846AE422…）；
一致性校验：磁盘裁切图数量与清单行数一致（309 = 309）；
中文渲染：matplotlib 用微软雅黑出图，中文标题/坐标轴无乱码；
编码兼容：CSV 统一 utf-8-sig，openpyxl 回读中文正确；
结果口径锁定：分类得分不依赖 Schema 合规（否则 A/B 组无法比较），
该口径由 test_evaluation.py 的用例固定，防止将来被无意改回。
## 10. 部署与运行说明
## 11. 项目局限性与后续改进
详见 docs/limitations.md 与 docs/experiment_report.md。要点：
1. 实测准确率仅 33%–38%（四分类随机水平 25%），不足以支撑生产使用；
2. 增加提示词约束改善了格式（JSON 有效率 0% → 99.5%），但没有提升准确率；
3. 模型的拒答机制在提示词层面完全未被触发（0/600），格式可控、可靠性不可控；
4. 测试集 200 条、sitting 仅 13 条，少数类指标方差大；
5. 输入是人工 bbox 裁切的单猪俯视图，不可与整帧多目标任务指标直接比较；
6. 单一模型、单次运行，未做重复实验与置信区间；
3. 单一模型、单次运行，未做稳定性重复（可用 --repeats 开启）；
4. 仅覆盖 2 个猪栏 8 台相机，跨场泛化未验证；
5. Python 3.9 与需求建议的 3.10+ 存在差异，已记录；
6. 后续：unseen-VP 划分泛化实验、sitting 过采样或自助法置信区间、
标注一致性 κ、多模型对照。

title: limitations.md
text:
# 局限性与适用边界
本文件说明本系统"能做什么、不能做什么、结论在什么范围内成立"。
所有条目均基于实际实现与实测结果，不做推测性夸大。
## 1. 数据规模与代表性
测试集来自公开数据集 anilbhujel/viewpoint-aware-pig-posture-recognition 的 seen-VP test
划分，通过逐实例 bbox 裁切得到单猪图像。样本量见 data/manifest.csv
（目标 120–200 条，实际数量以构建结果为准）。
类别严重不均衡：原划分中 sitting 仅占 2.7%（70/2603 实例）。
经过配额选图后，坐姿样本数仍然偏少，其 Precision/Recall/F1 的置信区间很宽，
不能据此断言模型"识别不了坐姿"，只能说明在本次样本量下表现如何。
数据来自 2 个猪栏、8 台固定相机（鱼眼 + RGB 深度相机），不覆盖其它猪场、
其它品种、其它光照与栏舍布局。跨场泛化能力未验证。
## 2. 裁切引入的先天偏差
本项目的输入是按人工 bbox 裁出的单只猪，而非原始整帧。
这意味着：
任务比"整帧多目标姿态识别"简单，指标不可与整帧检测任务的论文结果直接比较；
bbox 由数据集作者标注，若标注框偏紧或偏松，会影响模型可见的上下文。
同一源图的多个裁切被强制划入同一 split，避免近重复泄漏；但同帧样本仍共享
光照、背景与相机视角，统计独立性弱于同数量的独立拍摄图片。
## 3. 模型依赖
全部结果依赖单一云端模型（默认 glm-4.6v-flash）与单一供应商。
更换模型、甚至同一模型的版本更新，都可能改变结论。
因此实验元数据中记录了 model_name、提示词 SHA256、参数与时间戳；

title: limitations.md
text:
跨版本结果不应合并为同一轮对照实验（需求 6.3）。
免费模型可能存在限流、排队、静默降级等情况，本项目的响应时间包含网络与排队等待，
不等于模型的纯推理时延。
## 4. 提示词实验的边界
三组提示词（A 基础 / B 定义 / C 定义+结构化+不确定性）只在本测试集上比较一次，
没有做多次重复实验（可通过 --repeats 开启，但会增加调用量）。
因此两组之间的小幅差异可能落在噪声范围内，不应过度解读。
实测结果：A 0.377 / B 0.370 / C 0.330，三者差距（≤4.7 个百分点）在 200 样本上
接近噪声量级。三组预测完全相同的样本占 85%，说明提示词改变的主要是输出格式，
而不是判断本身。
一个反直觉的实测现象：定义最详细的 C 组准确率最低。可能原因是长定义强化了
对 lyinglateral 的先验（C 组 179/200 预测为侧卧）。不能据此断言"详细定义有害"**，
只能说在本任务、本模型、本视角下没有带来收益。
只有 A 组的输出格式最宽松，其"准确率"与"JSON 有效率"受到格式而非能力的
双重影响；报告中同时给出两个指标正是为了区分这一点，但仍难以完全解耦
（本项目已改为"分类得分不要求 Schema 合规"以缓解该问题）。
提示词语言固定为中文，未测试英文提示词的影响。
## 4.1 模型行为的实测局限
拒答机制未生效：C 组明确允许 unknown，但 600 次调用中拒答 0 次。
说明"靠提示词实现不确定性门控"在本模型上不可行。
类别塌缩：80%+ 的预测集中在 lying_lateral，sitting 一次未被预测。
这是模型先验，不是提示词能纠正的问题。

title: limitations.md
text:
视角是主要瓶颈：裁切图为正上方俯拍，四肢常被躯干遮挡；
目视复核显示部分误判样本在先验上确实难以单帧判断。
## 5. 指标口径的限制
unknown 的处理：主指标使用"有效分类子集"口径，同时给出"严格口径"
（拒答计为错误）与"无法判断比例"。只看 Accuracy(有效) 会高估能力，
必须结合拒答率一起看。
混淆矩阵中"调用失败"的样本不计入任何格子，只在失败率里体现。
响应时间仅统计成功调用。
样本量较小时，Macro-F1 对少数类的波动非常敏感。
## 6. 明确不支持的能力
以下内容不属于本项目的功能，系统输出也不应被这样使用：
❌ 背膘厚、肌内脂肪、体重、体尺的测量或估计；
❌ 疾病诊断、健康状态判定、用药建议；
❌ 多目标检测与个体身份识别（ReID）；
❌ 实时视频流分析与多摄像头联动；
❌ 生产级养殖场系统的可靠性保证（本项目为课程原型）。
模型的 description 字段只是可见体态的自然语言描述，不是专业评估结论。
## 7. 工程与合规限制
图片会通过公网发送至第三方模型服务商处理。不得上传未获授权的内部数据。
使用的数据集为 CC BY 4.0，报告中已注明出处与引用；再分发时须保留署名。
运行环境为 Python 3.9（低于需求建议的 3.10），未使用 3.10+ 语法；
未来升级解释器时需重新验证依赖兼容性。
未实现用户鉴权、多用户隔离、数据持久化数据库，仅适合单人本机使用。
## 8. 后续改进方向
1. 扩大到 unseen-VP 划分，量化跨相机视角的泛化损失；
2. 对 sitting 类做定向过采样，或在报告中给出自助法置信区间；
3. 引入第二次人工复核，报告标注一致性（Cohen's κ）；
4. 用 --repeats 做稳定性实验，区分"能力差异"与"采样噪声"；
5. 增加一个更强/更弱的对照模型，观察提示词收益是否依赖模型能力；
6. 把整帧多目标场景接入（需要目标检测，属于另一个任务）。

本目录存放实验用数据。图片不提交到 git（见 .gitignore），可通过

随机种子 20261019，dev 比例 0.2；
6. 写出图片与 manifest.csv / labels.csv，并做"磁盘图片数 = 清单行数"一致性校验。

# Viewpoint-Aware Pig Posture Recognition Dataset
This dataset supports multi-camera, viewpoint-aware pig posture recognition in livestock barn environments. It contains real-world pig images, bounding box annotations, posture class labels, and per-instance camera viewpoint angles (azimuth and elevation) derived from PnP-based camera calibration.

title: Viewpoint-Aware Pig Posture Recognition（数据集说明）
text:
Images were captured from 2 real-world pig pens using 4 cameras per pen — 2 overhead fisheye turret cameras and 2 RGB Orbbec depth cameras — installed at different positions and angles. This multi-viewpoint setting captures natural variation in how postures appear under different camera perspectives.
Each annotation includes:
A bounding box around an individual pig
A posture class label (5 classes)
Camera viewpoint angles (azimuth and elevation) for that pig's position
The source image filename and resolution
## Posture Classes
| Class ID | Label | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| 0 | Laterallyingleft | Pig lying on its side, left laterally |
| 1 | Laterallyingright | Pig lying on its side, right laterally |

| 2 | Sitting | Pig in sitting posture |
| 3 | Standing | Pig standing upright |
| 4 | Sternal_lying | Pig lying on sternum (chest-down, sphinx-like) |

## Viewpoint Angle Convention
Angles follow the zenith convention:
Azimuth (azimuth_deg): angle of the horizontal projection of the camera-to-pig ray, measured from the +X axis, counter-clockwise positive (−180° to +180°).

title: Viewpoint-Aware Pig Posture Recognition（数据集说明）
text:
Elevation (elevation_deg, zenith): 0° means the camera is directly overhead the pig; 90° means the camera is at the same height as the pig (horizontal line of sight).
The (sin, cos) encoding avoids angle-wrapping discontinuities and is used directly as the four-dimensional angle feature vector [azimuthsin, azimuthcos, elevationsin, elevationcos] in model training.

## Seen vs. Unseen Viewpoint Splits
The dataset is split to evaluate viewpoint generalisation:
Seen-VP test set: Images from the same camera positions that appear in training. Tests in-distribution performance.

title: Viewpoint-Aware Pig Posture Recognition（数据集说明）
text:
Unseen-VP test set: Images from camera positions held out from training. Tests how well the model generalises to new camera angles.
The large unseen-VP test set (11,708 instances) provides a realistic evaluation of cross-camera generalisation.
---
## Data Collection
Images were collected from pig barn environments using ceiling- and wall-mounted cameras. Pigs were annotated with bounding boxes and posture labels. Camera calibration parameters were estimated using the PnP algorithm applied to 4 manually annotated pen-floor corner points per camera, without requiring physical measurement of the pen dimensions.

text:
# Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
## Abstract

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: Posture detection targeted towards providing assessments for the monitoring of health and welfare of pigs has been of great interest to researchers from different disciplines. Existing studies applying machine vision techniques are mostly based on methods using three-dimensional imaging systems, or two-dimensional systems with the limitation of monitoring under controlled conditions. Thus, the main goal of this study was to determine whether a two-dimensional imaging system, along with deep learning approaches, could be utilized to detect the standing and lying (belly and side) postures of pigs under commercial farm conditions. Three deep learning-based detector methods, including faster regions with convolutional neural network features

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
(Faster R-CNN), single shot multibox detector (SSD) and region-based fully convolutional network (R-FCN), combined with Inception V2, Residual Network (ResNet) and Inception ResNet V2 feature extractions of RGB images were proposed. Data from different commercial farms were used for training and validation of the proposed models. The experimental results demonstrated that the R-FCN ResNet101 method was able to detect lying and standing postures with higher average precision (AP) of 0.93, 0.95 and 0.92 for standing, lying on side and lying on belly postures, respectively and mean average precision (mAP) of more than 0.93.
## 1. Introduction

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: Computer vision techniques, either three-dimensional (3D) or two-dimensional (2D), have been widely used in animal monitoring processes and play an essential role in assessment of animal behaviours. They offer benefits for the monitoring of farm animals due to the wide range of applications, cost and efficiency [1]. Examples of employing machine vision techniques in monitoring of animal health and behaviour have been reviewed [1,2,3]. In monitoring of pigs, interpretation of animal behaviours, particularly those relating to health and welfare as well as barn climate conditions, is strongly related to their locomotion and posture patterns [3,4]. In order to determine lying and standing postures in pigs, 3D cameras have been widely used, due

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: to their possibility of offering different colours in each pixel of an image based on the distance between the object and the depth sensor.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: One such effort was reported by [5], in which the monitoring of standing pigs was addressed by using the Kinect sensor. In this research, initially noise from depth images was removed by applying a spatiotemporal interpolation technique, then a background subtraction method was applied to detect standing pigs. Lao et al. [6] recognized lying, sitting and standing behaviours of sows based on 3D images. In another study, a Kinect sensor was also employed to localize standing pigs in depth images for automatic detection of aggressive events [7]. 2D images have also been used for locomotion and lying posture detection, which were mainly based on pixel movement [8] or features of ellipses fitted to the animals [9,10].

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: In most of the studies, due to different light sources and resolution (quality) of captured images, problems of a high level of noise and the generation of a great deal of data cause challenges for machine vision-based monitoring of livestock. It has been reported that machine learning techniques have the possibility to tackle these problems [11,12]. The most popular machine learning techniques employed for analysis of optical data for monitoring of pigs are included models (i.e., linear discriminant analysis (LDA), artificial neural networks (ANN), support vector machine (SVM)). However, in recent years, deep learning approaches, a fast-growing field of machine learning, have been used in image classification, object recognition,

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: localization and object detection [13]. Deep learning is similar to ANN, but with deeper architecture and the ability for massive learning capabilities which leads to higher performance [14]. Deep learning has recently been applied in 2D and 3D pig-based machine vision studies. An example is the separation of touching pigs in 3D images using a low-cost Kinect camera, based on the convolutional neural network (CNN), with high accuracy of around 92% [15].

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: Deep learning has also been used for detection and recognition of pigs’ or sows’ behaviours in different imaging systems. A detection system based on the Kinect v2 sensor, the faster regions with convolutional neural network features (Faster R-CNN) technique in combination with region proposal network (RPN) and Zeiler and Fergus Net (ZFnet), were developed by [16] to identify different postures of sows (i.e., standing and sitting behaviours, and sternal, ventral and lateral recumbency). Yang et al. [17] used deep learning for automatic recognition of sows’ nursing behaviours in 2D images, with an accuracy of 97.6%, sensitivity of 90.9% and specificity of 99.2%. Faster R-CNN and ZFnet were also employed to recognize individual feeding

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: behaviours of pigs by [18], where each pig in the barn was labelled with a letter. Their proposed method was able to recognise pigs’ feeding behaviours with an accuracy of 99.6% during the study. Segmentation of sow images from background in top view 2D images was also addressed by means of Fully Convolutional Network (FCN), built in Visual Geometry Group Network with 16 layers (VGG16), in another study by [19]. Their results showed the possibility of employing deep learning approaches for segmentation of the animal from different background conditions.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: Due to the fast growth of pig production around the world, the issue of real-time monitoring of the animals, particularly in large scale farms, becomes more crucial [1]. Monitoring of an individual pig’s posture during the whole lifetime in large scale farms is almost impossible for farmers or researchers, due to the labour- and time-intensive nature of the task. Utilizing state-of-the-art machine learning, along with machine vision techniques, for monitoring of groups of pigs in different farming conditions could offer the advantage of early problem detection, delivering better performance and lower costs. Thus, the main objective of this study was to develop a machine vision and a deep learning-based method to detect standing and lying

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
postures of individual pigs in different farming conditions, including a variety of commercial farm systems.
## 2. Material and Methods
## 2.1. Housing and Data Collection

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: The data sets for this study were derived from three different commercial farms in Germany and Sweden. In Germany, two farms for weaning and fattening of commercial hybrids of Pietrain× (Large White × Landrace) were selected. A set of four pens in a room in each farm were chosen; these had fully slatted floors with central concrete panels and plastic panels on both sides (weaning farm), and fully slatted concrete floors (fattening farm). In a Swedish fattening farm, two rooms with two pens were selected, each having part-slatted concrete flooring with some litter on the solid concrete in the lying area. Pigs were of commercial Hampshire × (Landrace × Large White) breeding.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
The images used in this study were recorded by top view cameras (VIVOTEK IB836BA-HF3, and Hikvision DS-2CD2142FWD-I). The cameras were connected via cables to servers and video images from the cameras were recorded simultaneously and stored on hard disks. Recording in different farming conditions allowed for capture of images with pigs of different skin colour and age, housed under various floor type and illumination conditions, which facilitated the development of a robust deep learning model. Examples of images used for development of the detection model are illustrated in Figure 1.
## 2.2. Proposed Methodology

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: According to the findings of Nasirahmadi et al. [12], when in a side (lateral) lying posture pigs lie in a fully recumbent position with limbs extended, and when in a belly (sternal) lying posture the limbs are folded under the body. Due to the lack of available benchmark datasets for pigs’ lying and standing postures, three classes of standing, lying on belly and lying on side were defined in this work. Examples of these postures are represented in Figure 2. Most of the possible scenarios of individual pig standing and lying postures within the group have been considered. The proposed detection methods were developed and implemented in python 3.6 and OpenCV 3.4 using TensorFlow [20]. Experiments and the deep learning training were conducted on a Windows 10 with a NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 GPU with 6GB of memory.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: In order to establish the lying and standing postures, images from the three commercial farms over a period of one year were collected from surveillance videos. A total of 4900 images (4500 for training and validation, and 400 for testing) from this dataset, which incorporated various farm, animal age, and animal and background colour conditions, were selected to provide the training (80%: 3600) and validation (20%: 900) datasets. The images were selected at 1–2 week intervals from the beginning to the end of every batch, and different samples of images were collected randomly in one day of these selected weeks. Furthermore, another 400 images were taken randomly from the image data set as a testing set. The testing data were independent

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: of the training and validation sets, and were used for an evaluation of the detection phase. All images were first resized to 1280 × 720 (width × height), then annotated using the graphical image annotation tool LabelImg, created by [21]. The annotations included the identification of standing and lying postures and were saved as XML files in the PASCAL VOC format. Since each image included different pigs (7–32 in number) based on farm conditions and time of recording, the total number of labelled postures was 52,785. The information on each posture class is summarized in Table 1.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: In this study, various combinations of deep learning-based models (i.e., Faster R-CNN (Inception V2, ResNet50, ResNet101 and Inception-ResNet V2), R-FCN (ResNet101) and SSD (Inception V2)) were developed with the aim of finding the best posture detection technique in 2D images. Two architectures of the ResNet model (i.e., ResNet50 and ResNet101) were applied. ResNet is a deep residual network introduced by [22] and has been widely used in object detection and localization tasks. Both ResNet50 and ResNet101 are based on repeating of four residual blocks. These feature extractors are made of three convolution layers of 1 × 1, 3 × 3 and 1 × 1. They also have an additional connection joining the input of the first 1 × 1 convolution layer to the output of the last convolution 1 × 1 layer.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: Additionally, residual learning in the ResNet model resolves the training by fusing filtered features with original features. ResNet50 and 101 are very deep networks and contain 50 and 101 layers. ResNet applies skip connections and batch normalization and provides short connection between layers [23]. Furthermore, ResNets allow direct signal propagation from the first to the end layer of the network without the issue of degradation. Inception V2 GoogLeNet [24] with layer-by-layer structure was also implemented as a feature extractor of the input pig posture images. The feature extractors which map input images to feature maps, characterize computational cost as well as performance of networks. Inception V2 GoogLeNet is based on the repetition of building blocks and extracts features concatenated as output of the module [24].

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: It is made of a pooling layer and different convolutional layers. The convolution layers are of different sizes of 1 × 1, 3 × 3, 5 × 5 and help to extract features from the same feature map on different scales and improve performance. Inception V2, by factorization of filters n×n to a combination of 1 × n and n × 1 convolutions, has led to better performance and reduction in representational bottlenecks. This has resulted in the widening of the filter banks instead of deepening, to remove the representational bottleneck without increase in computational cost and number of parameters [25]. Finally, Inception-ResNet V2, which was proposed in 2017 [26], was utilized as a feature extractor in this work. Inception-ResNet V2 is one of the

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
state-of-the-art approaches in image classification and is based on combination of residual connections and Inception architectures. Inception-ResNet V2 is an Inception style network which uses residual connections instead of filter concatenation [26]. Further details on all parameters of the proposed feature extractors can be found in [22,24,26].
## 2.2.1. Faster R-CNN

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: The Faster R-CNN method [27] was used to monitor standing, side and belly lying postures of pigs. Figure 3 shows the architecture and different steps of the Faster R-CNN utilized in posture detection. Various feature extraction methods (Inception V2, ResNet50, ResNet101 and Inception-ResNet V2) were applied and the regional proposal network (RPN), which is a fully convolutional network for generating object proposals, was used to produce a proposed region for each image and generate feature maps in the final layer by predicting the classes [25]. The feature maps were fed into the region of interest (RoI) pooling to extract regions from the last feature maps. Each RoI (region of pigs) was then determined to a confidence score. Finally, the

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
feature vector from the RoI was fed into several fully connected (FC) layers of a softmax classifier to obtain the final assurance scores and a regression bounding box to localize the coordinates of the detected objects.
## 2.2.2. R-FCN

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: R-FCN [28] is an improvement of the Faster R-CNN and is proposed as an object detection technique using CNNs. The structure of the proposed R-FCN applied in this study is shown in Figure 4. The R-FCN consists of a feature extractor (ResNet101 in this study) and several FC layers behind an RoI pooling layer. The RoI pooling layer uses position sensitive maps to address the issue of translation invariance [29]. In the R-FCN, the computation is shared across the whole image by creating a deeper FCN without increasing the speed overhead. Region proposal and classification are done by use of RPN, followed by the position sensitive maps and RoI pooling, respectively. For training of the R-FCN model in this study, the same hyperparameters as the

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
faster R-CNN were used.
## 2.2.3. SSD
The SSD was proposed by Liu et al. [30] and is based on a bounding box regression principle. In the SSD, the input images are first divided into small kernels on different feature maps to predict anchor boxes of each kernel (Figure 5). In comparison with the Faster R-CNN and R-FCN techniques, SSD uses a single feed forward CNN to produce a series of bounding boxes and scores for the presence of the objects in each box [29]. Finally, the classification scores of each region are computed based on the score obtained in the previous section. The SSD model, instead of applying proposal generation, encloses the whole process into a single network, which leads to less computational time.
The initial learning rate is a hyperparameter and shows adjustment of weight of the networks.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: Too high learning rates may cause poor converge or a network unable to converge, and a low initial learning rate will result in slow convergence [31]. So, in this study different initial learning rates of 0.03, 0.003, 0.0003 were selected to train the Faster R-CNN, R-FCN and SSD networks. The momentum algorithm accumulates the weighted average of the previous training gradient and continues to move in that direction. The past weighted average updates the current gradient direction, and the momentum coefficient specifies to what extent the update needs to increase or decrease [32]. In this study, training of all networks was conducted with a momentum 0.9. The right number of iterations is important in training of the models, as too small

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
numbers will result in poor performance while a high number of iterations may cause a weakening of the generalization ability of the trained model [32]. So, according to the number of samples [32] the iteration number, which shows the number of weight updates during the training process, was chosen to be 70,000 for all networks in this study. Furthermore, for data augmentation a random horizontal flip method for all detectors was used.
## 3. Experimental Results and Discussion

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: The big challenges in monitoring of pigs’ behaviour, particularly in large-scale farms, are cost, time and labour-intensity of the visual investigation. The importance of automatic monitoring of group and individual behaviours of pigs has led to the development of image processing techniques with the ability to monitor a large number of pigs. However, due to the variability in farm and animal conditions, especially in commercial farms, the development of a robust monitoring technique with the ability to detect individual animal behaviours has been examined in this study.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: The performance obtained for each posture class of the models in the test data set with each initial learning rate is illustrated in Table 2. In order to evaluate the detection capability of the proposed models, the widely used average precision (AP) of each class and mean average precision (mAP) were calculated. High values for the AP and mAP show the acceptable performance of the R-FCN ResNet101, Faster R-CNN ResNet 101 and Faster R-CNN Inception V2 detection approaches for scoring of standing, lying on belly and lying on side postures among group-housed pigs when compared to the other models. Additionally, the learning rate of 0.003 gave the best results in the mentioned detection models. The evaluation metrics illustrate a trend for

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: improvement when the learning rate decreases from 0.03 to 0.003, however these values declined at the learning rate of 0.0003. This finding is in line with the previous finding that the detection performance changes with the same trend in learning rates in various scenarios [33].

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: The training and validation loss of the models at a learning rate of 0.003 are presented in Figure 6. As can be seen, there are more fluctuations in the validation curves than in the training ones for each model, which could be due to the lower size of data set used in the validation phase [34]. The graphs show the decrease in the loss of training and validation steps of the developed models, and the values converged at a low value when the training process was finished, which is an indicator of a sufficiently trained process. After training the model, 400 images (not used for training and validation) were used as a test set (including 4987 lying and standing postures) to evaluate the correctness of the posture detection approaches. The

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
test data set contained images from the three farms of the study which were selected from different times of the day where animals had lying, feeding, drinking and locomotion activities in the barn.
Figure 7 illustrates examples of detected postures by Faster R-CNN, R-FCN and SSD models in the different farming conditions in the learning rate of 0.003. As can be seen from the figure, some of the developed algorithms have the ability to detect different lying and standing postures under all tested commercial farming conditions. In some cases, there were multiple postures in an image, so the possibility of detecting various postures in an image is also shown in Figure 7.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
It can be observed from Table 2 that one of the major misdetections was with respect to standing and belly lying postures. Due to the similarity between these postures in top view images (Figure 8), some incorrect detection was observed. However, in lying on side the animals have a different top view image (Figure 2) compared to the other postures, and the number of incorrect detections was lower.
The confusion matrix of the selected R-FCN ResNet101 model in the test dataset is shown in Table 3. As can be seen in the table, the number of misdetections between standing and belly lying postures are higher than the other postures.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: The proposed R-FCN ResNet101 technique for detection of standing and lying postures in pigs under commercial farming conditions by 2D cameras provided a high level of detection performance (e.g., mAP of 0.93), which is illustrated in Figure 7. In a sow posture study, Faster R-CNN along with RPN and ZF-net models were able to detect standing, sitting and lying behaviours with a mAP of 0.87 using Kinect v2 depth images [16]. In another study, monitoring of lying and nursing behaviour of sows using a deep learning approach (FCN and VGG16) resulted in achieved accuracy, sensitivity and specificity of 96.4%, 92.0% and 98.5%, respectively [17]. However, the study reported by [17] was carried out to monitor one sow per image, which has less probability of detection mistake compared to our study with number of pigs varying from 7–32 per image.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: The use of Faster R-CNN as a detector and ZF-net as a feature extractor showed high values of precision and recall (99.6% and 86.93%, respectively) in a study by [18]. However, compared to our study, they had just four animals in each image and each animal’s body was labelled as A, B, C, and D for tracking their behaviours, which would help to improve detection performance. There were some misdetections of the test data set for each posture in our study. This was mainly due to the similarity between standing and belly lying postures in top view images (Figure 8, as previously discussed) and to the problem of covering of the camera lens with fly dirt as time progressed, reducing the visibility in images [10]. Furthermore, the shape change

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: of an animal’s body caused by the fisheye lens effect at the edge of the pen (particularly in the weaning farm), and the existence of a water pipe in the middle of the pen (at the fattening farm) which caused some invisible area in the image, gave some misdetection in the models. Low resolution of the image data impacts on the performance of machine vision techniques, and the model is not able to extract enough features to perform accurate detection. As shown in this study, misdetection was more likely for pigs with black skin colour as they have a greater similarity with the background (pen floor) colour.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: Furthermore, in this study testing time of the state-of-the-art detection models was calculated. The speed of each proposed method was measured based on the frames per second (FPS) [35]. The results show a FPS of 6.4 for the Faster R-CNN Inception V2, 3.6 for the Faster R-CNN ResNet50, 3.8 for the Faster R-CNN ResNet101, 2.3 for the Faster R-CNN Inception-ResNet V2, 5 for the R-FCN ResNet101, and 8.8 for the proposed SSD Inception V2. According to Table 2, R-FCN ResNet101 showed the highest performance as well as an acceptable FPS (5) for the pig posture detection. It was also found that the Faster R-CNN Inception V2 had high enough performance for lying-on-side posture detection along with a FPS of 6.4. Since the lying posture can be used

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: as a parameter of pig comfort assessment in various thermal conditions, the Faster R-CNN Inception V2 model can be beneficial in terms of higher processing speed. The SSD model had the highest rate of FPS (8.8), however the lowest performance was obtained in this model, which was not sufficiently reliable in pig lying and standing detection.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: The proposed R-FCN model could be used to monitor pig postures in the group to control climate and barn conditions continuously. In this context, three days of recorded video data were fed into the model in order to score the number of the lying and standing postures. Results of the scoring phase are shown in Figure 9. Data from early morning (5:50) until evening (16:00), which includes different animals’ activities, were utilised and the number of the postures continuously saved in excel files.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: As shown in the scoring diagrams, the algorithm can continuously monitor the activity and postures of group-housed pigs in the barn. In the graph of standing postures, activity peaks were apparent at feeding and activity times or when the animals were checked by the farmer. The lying and standing activity patterns of the animals, which were scored using the proposed automated method, offer the advantage of early detection of health and welfare issues in pig farms [3]. For example, changes in lying and standing activities levels could be used for the detection of lameness and tail biting events [36].

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: In a previous study, Nasirahmadi et al. [12] showed that image processing and a linear SVM model was able to score different lying postures (sternal and lateral) in commercial farming conditions. However, the performance of the scoring technique was highly dependent on the output of the image processing method, which led to some wrong scoring in the pigs lying postures. In this study, due to the use of different deep learning approaches, high enough precision for practical use was obtained. The monitoring approach described in this study could be a valuable tool to detect changes in the number of pigs in the standing, lying on side or belly postures to improve welfare and health surveillance. However, this new method needs to be adapted

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text:
and evaluated with a wider range of farming conditions (both commercial and research) in future, which may require a greater number of images for training of the model or use of other feature extraction methods.
## 4. Conclusions

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: In pig husbandry, it is important to monitor the animals’ behaviour continuously between birth and slaughter. However, this can only be achieved using robust machine learning and machine vision techniques capable of processing image data from varied farming conditions. In this study, two commercial farms (weaning and fattening) in Germany and one commercial fattening farm in Sweden were used to record 2D video data for a year and provide an image database. In order to have various imaging conditions, pens with different floor type and colour, various numbers of pigs per pen (from 7 to 32) and varying ages and colours of pig were selected. The techniques proposed in this study were based on using image data from the surveillance system and Faster R-CNN, R-FCN and SSD methods.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: These models were trained using 80% (3600) of the image data and validated by 20% (900) of the 2D images, with a total of around 52,785 standing, lying on belly and lying on side postures in the images. The trained model was then evaluated using 400 new images. Results of the testing phase showed a high level of mAP and good processing speed for the different postures in the R-FCN ResNet101 model. This technique performed well in the monitoring of various lying and standing postures of pigs in image data acquired from commercial farms, which has been the limitation of most 2D and 3D conventional machine vision techniques. The proposed model has the flexibility and good robustness toward different pig farm lighting conditions, age of the

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Approaches for Posture Detection of Individual Pigs
text: animals and skin colour, which can be an important step toward developing real-time, continuous computer-based monitoring of livestock farms.

# Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
## Abstract
This study explored an image-based method for recognizing pigs’ postures during growth and established the world’s first human-annotated pig-posture-recognition dataset, which includes pigs standing, lying, lying on their sides, and exploring (the four common postures). Finally, the pig postures were judged, and good results were obtained in practical applications.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: Posture changes in pigs during growth are often precursors of disease. Monitoring pigs’ behavioral activities can allow us to detect pathological changes in pigs earlier and identify the factors threatening the health of pigs in advance. Pigs tend to be farmed on a large scale, and manual observation by keepers is time consuming and laborious. Therefore, the use of computers to monitor the growth processes of pigs in real time, and to recognize the duration and frequency of pigs’ postural changes over time, can prevent outbreaks of porcine diseases. The contributions of this article are as follows: (1) The first human-annotated pig-posture-identification dataset in the world was established, including 800 pictures of each of the four pig

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text:
postures: standing, lying on the stomach, lying on the side, and exploring. (2) When using a deep separable convolutional network to classify pig postures, the accuracy was 92.45%. The results show that the method proposed in this paper achieves adequate pig-posture recognition in a piggery environment and may be suitable for livestock farm applications.
## 1. Introduction

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: According to the National Bureau of Statistics of China, China is a major consumer of pork. A total of 544.19 million live pigs were sold in 2019 in China, accounting for 45.08% of the total sold globally and ranking China first in the world for pig sales [1]. In 2017, the output value of pig feeding in China was nearly 1.3 trillion yuan, accounting for about 56.5% of the total output value of domestic livestock and poultry (pigs, cattle, sheep and poultry) [2]. With an increase in the scale of the pig breeding industry, the possibility of swine diseases also increases. A failure to intervene or eliminate these hidden dangers over time may cause serious economic and human losses. For example, African Swine Fever (ASF), which has had a huge

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: impact on the world in recent years, is a virulent, infectious swine disease caused by the ASF virus, which is clinically characterized by acute febrile hemorrhage, high morbidity, and high mortality [3].

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: It poses a serious danger to the development of the pig industry. An epidemic not only incurs great economic losses for the affected country but also hampers international trade. Many diseases that may occur in the growth of live pigs are accompanied by changes in their postures before other subclinical and clinical symptoms emerge, which, at the same time, lead to changes in various external physiological parameters, such as decreased daily activities, a loss of appetite, and changes in their cries. Monitoring pigs’ posture can reveal the precursors of swine disease in a timely manner, identify the factors threatening the health of pigs in advance, detect and control the source of infection, and reduce the scope of infection, which will

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text:
help to slow down the transmission of severe infectious diseases in the pig population [4].
Secondly, the traditional pig industry requires breeders to obtain real-time information about the statuses of pigs so as to detect abnormalities, but the traditional observation method is time consuming and laborious, and interferes with the normal growth of pigs. At present, some breeders observe the statuses of pigs by watching surveillance videos, but this is time consuming, and, in most cases, breeders cannot accurately identify the postures of pigs.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: In recent years, technology led production systems have developed rapidly. For example, radio frequency identification (RFID) technology is now being used to identify the individual characteristics of pigs [5], and microinertial sensors are being used to monitor pig posture [6]. Various sensors, such as those for pressure, water volume, and acceleration, are also used to monitor lameness, drinking water, movement, and other postures [7,8,9]. However, these methods all rely on wearable hardware. In practical applications, sensors used at close range in denser piggeries are prone to damage or falling off.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: With the development of deep-learning technology, image processing has been gradually enhanced. It is mostly applied for animal-posture recognition in animal husbandry [10]. For example, Leroy et al. automatically recognized the standing, walking, and scratching postures of a single laying hen through a distribution model that used the elliptical fitting of points to measure the contours of laying hens [11]. Jiazhen Han used the Densenet model to realize the multi-label classification of dairy goat datasets [12]. However, most of these methods are based on individual identification, while in pig breeding, group breeding is the main method used and the pigs are generally clustered close together. L Zhang et al. used key point tracking,

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: triangulation, and other methods to detect multiple pigs. This type of method solves the problem of occlusion between pigs. In most production environments, background factors in the collected images greatly impact the recognition effect, and this effect is not ideal after image marginalization processing.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: Object detection is an important research direction in computer vision. Its purpose is to accurately identify the category and location of a specific target object in a given image. In recent years, the feature learning and transfer learning capabilities of deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN) have significantly progressed in the feature extraction, image expression, classification, and recognition for object-detection algorithms [13]. Image-segmentation technology is a process that involves dividing an image into several regions with different characteristics based on the principle of similarity, while semantic image segmentation is based on common pixel points and processes images at the pixel level [14]. These two methods have also

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: been applied in many agricultural fields in recent years. For example, Huimin Liao used the RGB-D (RGB+ Depth Map) method to segment individual images from groups [15], while Xiangze Lin used Mask R-CNN to quickly locate and identify rice planthoppers [16]. Though the target-detection method has a high recognition speed, it cannot remove the influence of the background. However, the semantic-segmentation method can segment the target completely.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: In order to make pig-posture recognition more accurate, this study established the world’s first human-annotated pig-posture-recognition dataset, including four pig postures: standing, lying on the stomach, lying on the side, and exploring. All the experiments described in this paper were based on this dataset.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: To solve the abovementioned problems, this paper proposes a hybrid model that combines object detection and semantic segmentation. First, we used the YOLOv5 object-detection method to extract individual pigs from pig-group pictures, and then, we used the DeepLab v3+ semantic-segmentation method to extract the individual contours of the pigs. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper adequately recognizes the postures of pigs in a piggery environment. The overall framework of the method is shown in Figure 1.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text:
This paper is divided into five sections. This section introduces the significance and objectives of pig-posture research. The second section describes the network principles used and compared in this paper. The third section specifically introduces the dataset and explains the image-preprocessing method. The fourth section describes the training process and experimental results for target extraction and classification, and analyzes the results obtained with different processing methods. The fifth section summarizes the findings and makes suggestions for future research.
## 2. Related Work
## 2.1. YOLOv5-Based Detection Network for a Single Pig

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
section: 2.1. YOLOv5-Based Detection Network for a Single Pig
text: Object detection is a form of image segmentation based on the geometric and statistical features of a target that also combines the segmentation and recognition of the target. The current deep-learning methods in the field of object detection are mainly divided into two categories. The one-stage target-detection algorithm is an end-to-end process, no candidate frames are required, and the positioning problem of the target frame is directly transformed via regression-problem processing, such as YOLO [17] or SSD [18]. The two-stage object-detection algorithm is based on the candidate area: the algorithm first generates a series of candidate frames as samples and then classifies the samples through the convolutional neural network. In the

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
section: 2.1. YOLOv5-Based Detection Network for a Single Pig
text: early stage of the development of end-to-end algorithms, such as YOLOv1, speed is the main advantage, while methods based on the candidate region have an advantage in terms of detection accuracy and precision.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
section: 2.1. YOLOv5-Based Detection Network for a Single Pig
text: However, YOLOv1 has the following two shortcomings: (1) Due to the output layer for the fully connected layer, in the test, the YOLO training model only supports and trains at the same input-image resolution. (2) Although each grid can predict the B bounding boxes, only the bounding box with the highest intersection over union (IoU) is selected as the object detection output; that is, each grid can only predict one object at most. When objects occupy a small proportion of the picture, such as when the image contains a flock of birds, each grid contains multiple objects, but only one of them can be detected [17]. YOLOv2 proposed a new training method: the joint training method. The basic idea is to train the object detector on both the

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
section: 2.1. YOLOv5-Based Detection Network for a Single Pig
text:
detection and classification datasets at the same time, to learn the exact position of the object with the data from the detection dataset, and to increase the number of categories and improve the robustness of the data from the classification dataset [19]. YOLOv3 introduces multi-scale prediction, and independently performs detection on the fusion feature maps of multiple scales, ultimately improving the detection effect of small targets significantly [20]. YOLOV4 [21] and YOLOV5 have a greatly improved training speed and accuracy, so this study adopted YOLOV5 as the first step of the joint training method.
## 2.2. DeepLabv3+-Based Edge-Extraction Network for a Single Pig

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
section: 2.2. DeepLabv3+-Based Edge-Extraction Network for a Single Pig
text: Image segmentation is another basic task in computer vision, in addition to classification and detection. It involves segmenting the picture into different blocks according to the content. DeepLab is a semantic-segmentation model proposed by Google. It improves the feature extractor of the convolutional neural network (CNN), which can model objects more successfully and interpret contextual information more accurately [22]. DeepLabv3+ is the latest improvement to the DeepLab model [23]. The main body of the DeepLabv3+ Encoder is DCNN with dilated convolutions. Common classification networks such as Resnet and Xception can be used, followed by atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) with dilated convolutions, to control the receptive field

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
section: 2.2. DeepLabv3+-Based Edge-Extraction Network for a Single Pig
text:
without changing the size of the feature map, which is beneficial for the extraction of multi-scale information. Compared with DeepLabv3, the direct bilinear interpolation to the original image size after the 1 × 1 classification layer is not conducive to obtaining finer segmentation results [24]. V3 + introduces a new DECODER module to further integrate low-level features with high-level features in order to improve the accuracy of the segmentation boundaries.
## 2.3. Feature-Extraction Network
## 2.3.1. Resnet

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text:
Resnet is a convolutional neural network proposed by Kaiming He from Microsoft Research, alongside three other people. It won the prize for image classification and object recognition as part of the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC) in 2015 [25]. The characteristics of this residual network include the fact that it is easy to optimize and the fact that it can increase the accuracy of recognition with the addition of considerable depth. The internal residual block uses jump connections, which alleviate the problem of the vanishing gradient caused by increasing depth in a deep neural network. An overview of the residual network is shown in Figure 2.
## 2.3.2. Xception

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text:
Xception [26] is another Google modification of Inception-V3 [27]. The author of [26] believes that the correlation between channels and the spatial correlation should be handled separately. Therefore, depthwise separable convolution is also used to replace the convolution operation in Inception-v3, which can improve the effect of the model with only a small increase in network complexity.
## 2.3.3. MobileNet

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: In 2012, AlexNet won the first prize in the ImageNet competition [28]. Since then, even deeper neural networks have been proposed, such as the excellent VGG series, GoogleNet, and the Resnet series. However, as these networks become deeper, the huge storage pressure and computing overheads caused by model computation begin to seriously affect the application of deep neural networks in some low-power fields, such as Resnet152 in the Resnet series, where the network layer reached 152 layers and the weight of the model reached hundreds of megabytes.

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text:
MobileNet is a network architecture that was released by Google in 2017. It is a convolutional neural network with a small model volume, fewer training parameters, and fewer requirements for computation [29]. Aimed at making full use of limited computing resources and maximizing the accuracy of the model, it is one of the models most commonly deployed in edge computing. The main innovation of MobileNet is the replacement of regular convolution with depthwise separable convolution and the use of a width multiplier to reduce the number of parameters. In addition, it can achieve better data throughput with only a minimal cost to its precision.

## 3. Materials and Methods
## 3.1. Dataset

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: The pictures used in this study are from the Sichuan Wangjiang Farming Muli Base. The dataset was captured by the surveillance camera in the base, with a resolution of 1920 × 1080 pixels, which was located on the upper side of the pig house, shooting at about 45 degrees from top to bottom. The videos were taken from October to November 2020. Frames were extracted based on 2 s intervals. Most of the images in the dataset are clear, though some pigs in a few images were blurry when static images were captured due to movement. In this study, such images were also added to the dataset in order to increase its robustness. The dataset marked the position of each pig whose posture could be clearly judged, as well as the positions of any pigs

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text:
visible at the edges of the frame, and marked four common postures, including standing, lying on the stomach, lying on the side, and exploring. Finally, this article collected 1550 multi-target object detection images, and further segmented the datasets into the standing, lying on the side, lying on the side, and exploring categories, leading to a total of 3200 images in the detection results. The detection and classification datasets were divided into training and testing sets at a ratio of 7:3.
## 3.2. Image Pre-Processing
## 3.2.1. Single-Target Extraction by Target Detection

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: This paper used the YOLOv5 network to extract a single target from the input multi-pig images. There are four versions of the object detection network given by YOLOV5, which are YOLOv5s, YOLOv5m, YOLOv5l, and YOLOv5x. The goal of this step was to detect a single pig body as quickly as possible. We tested YOLOv5 on the constructed dataset. YOLOv5s showed the fastest speed and relatively high accuracy, so we chose it as the model for this step. The multi-angle single-pig image size was adjusted to 608 × 608 through adaptive image scaling, and it was sent to the network. The original 608 × 608 × 3 image was input into the newly added focus structure; first, it was turned into a feature map of 304 × 304 × 12 by using the slicing operation, and

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text:
then, it became a feature map of 304 × 304 × 32 after a convolution operation with 32 convolution kernels. After the input into the structure of feature pyramid networks (FPN) combined with the path aggregation network (PAN), GIoU_Loss was used as the loss function of the bounding box frame to perform the final target detection. title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: In order to enhance the effectiveness of the feature extraction and the accuracy of algorithm recognition, image pre-processing was performed on single-target pictures before semantic-segmentation training. In order to solve the problem of jaggy edges in the test set for semantic segmentation, non-local means (NL-means) filtering [30] was used to denoise the image. The algorithm used redundant information commonly found in natural images to remove noise. ## 3.3. DeepLabv3+ Network Structure

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: In DeepLab v3+, Liang-Chieh Chen et al. used an encoder–decoder to perform multi-scale information fusion while retaining the original dilated convolutions and ASPP layer. Its backbone network uses the Xception model, which improves the robustness and operating speed of semantic segmentation [23]. DeepLabv3+’s network structure is shown in Figure 5. It achieved a mean intersection over union (MIoU) of 89.0% on Pascal VOC, and an MIoU of 82.1% on Cityscape. The greatest improvement of DeepLab v3+ is to regard the DCNN part of DeepLab as an encoder, and up-sample the feature map output by DCNN into the part of the original image size regarded as a decoder, which constitutes the encoder–decoder system. Bilinear interpolation up-sampling is a

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration

title: Pig-Posture Recognition Based on Computer Vision: Dataset and Exploration
text: By experimenting with DeepLab v3 and DeepLab v3+, this study discovered that, when the original DeepLab v3 uses the backbone Resnet-101, the feature map of the subsequent nine layers becomes larger, the amount of calculation greatly increases, and dealing with high-resolution images is time consuming [23]. On this basis, DeepLab v3+ uses modified aligned Xception’s improved Resnet-101, and uses 1 × 1 convolution to reduce the number of channels from low-level features. By inputting the noise-reduced pig pictures into the network where Resnet-101, MobileNet, and Xception are the backbone, after experimental feedback, Resnet-101 shows the best effect.
